q: מטופלת בת 82 מגיעה לבית חולים עם שברים חוזרים שאינם מוסברים היטב. לפי נוהל משרד הבריאות לטיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, מהי הגישה המתאימה?
o: לברר את החשד לאחר קבלת הוכחה לזהותו של הגורם לשברים
לברר את החשד ביחידות ובשיתוף עובד סוציאלי
לברר את החשד לאחר הגשת תלונה רשמית של המטופלת למשטרה
לברר את החשד בנוכחות המלווה ובאמצעות תשאול משותף
explanation:
סימנים לפגיעה מחייבים בירור דיסקרטי ופעולה להגנה. לא צריך לזהות בוודאות את הפוגע לפני שמתחילים. **לברר את החשד ביחידות ובשיתוף עובד סוציאלי**.

**א. לברר את החשד לאחר קבלת הוכחה לזהותו של הגורם לשברים.** הוכחת זהות הפוגע אינה תנאי לבדיקה.
**ב. לברר את החשד ביחידות ובשיתוף עובד סוציאלי.** פרטיות ועו״ס מאפשרים להעריך את הפגיעה ואת הצורך בהגנה.
**ג. לברר את החשד לאחר הגשת תלונה רשמית של המטופלת למשטרה.** אין להתנות עזרה בהגשת תלונה מצד המטופלת.
**ד. לברר את החשד בנוכחות המלווה ובאמצעות תשאול משותף.** תשאול בנוכחות המלווה עלול להרתיע אותה מלספר.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, עמ׳ 6 ונספח 1, עמ׳ 8.
ref: משרד הבריאות, חוזר המנהל הכללי 22/03: נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות

o: ירידה סנסוריניוראלית בשמיעה הקשורה להזדקנות, במיוחד בתדירויות גבוהות
ירידת שמיעה הולכתית
ירידת שמיעה חד-צדדית פתאומית
טינטון בלבד
explanation:
פרסביאקוזיס היא **ירידת שמיעה תחושתית־עצבית הקשורה להזדקנות, בעיקר בתדרים גבוהים**. היא מתפתחת לרוב בהדרגה ובשתי האוזניים ועלולה להתבטא בקושי בהבנת דיבור בתנאי רעש.

**א. ירידה תחושתית־עצבית הקשורה לגיל.** שינויים בשבלול ובמערכת השמיעה פוגעים בהבחנה בין צלילים. אודיומטריה מסייעת לאפיין את הירידה ולהתאים שיקום.
**ב. ירידה הולכתית.** חסימה בתעלה או מחלה של עור התוף או האוזן התיכונה משבשות את הולכת הקול, במנגנון אחר.
**ג. ירידה חד־צדדית פתאומית.** זהו דפוס המחייב בירור דחוף אם מדובר באובדן תחושתי־עצבי, ולא התפתחות הדרגתית טיפוסית.
**ד. טינטון בלבד.** טינטון עשוי להתלוות לירידה בשמיעה, אך אינו תחליף להדגמת ליקוי שמיעה.

אסמכתא · Hazzard 8e, עמ׳ 490, 494–495, 499. Lin, NEJM, 2024, עמ׳ 1505–1508.
ref: Hazzard Ch 34 — HEARING LOSS: ASSESSMENT AND MANAGEMENT

q: An 82-year-old man with COPD, heart failure, and diabetes is hospitalized for an acute exacerbation. His family asks the team to “do everything,” although he previously said he did not want to be kept alive by machines. The team presents options mainly in terms of survival statistics and technical procedures. What is the main limitation of this communication approach?
o: It should use the family’s request as the main treatment-selection criterion
It should connect treatment outcomes with the patient’s values and preferences
It should replace prognostic discussion with procedural descriptions for the family
It should set aside prior patient statements when the current situation differs
explanation:
A serious-illness conversation should explain what a procedure would mean for the patient's lived outcome. **Connect survival estimates and treatment options to his values and prior wish about machines**.

**A. Family request alone.** Clarify what “everything” means and what the patient wanted.
**B. Outcomes and values.** Explore which outcomes he would consider worth the burdens of treatment.
**C. More procedural detail alone.** Technical descriptions cannot show whether treatment fits the person's goals.
**D. Ignore earlier statements.** Past wishes are relevant, even when their application to current circumstances requires discussion.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1103, 1102.

q: A 78-year-old woman attends routine follow-up. She reports unintentional loss of 4 kg in six months, increased exhaustion, and difficulty walking to her mailbox without resting. She has hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and osteoarthritis. Examination finds reduced grip strength and slow gait. Her medication regimen is stable, and she has no acute medical illness. Which interpretation follows Hazzard's description of the Fried frailty phenotype?
o: The combination warrants assessment of a multisystem frailty syndrome
The weak grip establishes frailty independently of the other clinical findings
The chronic diagnoses establish frailty independently of the physical features
The absence of an acute precipitant makes a frailty assessment unnecessary
explanation:
Frailty can develop gradually while chronic diseases appear stable. **Exhaustion, slow walking and reduced grip together warrant formal assessment for the physical frailty phenotype.**

**A. Assess the multisystem syndrome** — Measure grip and gait against the appropriate thresholds, ask about usual activity and clarify the weight-loss history. The findings are more informative together.
**B. Weak grip alone** — Weakness supplies a single component. Three of five components define the frail category.
**C. Chronic diagnoses alone** — Hypertension, diabetes and osteoarthritis may affect function, but their presence does not score the Fried phenotype.
**D. Wait for an acute precipitant** — The phenotype identifies susceptibility before a stressor occurs, when there is still an opportunity to discuss function and risk.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 619–620, Table 42-2.

q: A healthy, active 70-year-old woman has persistent urgency incontinence despite behavioral treatment and trials of several anticholinergic drugs over the past year. She wants a minimally invasive option before considering major surgery. Which procedure is described for refractory urgency incontinence?
o: Surgical bladder neck suspension
Periurethral collagen injection
Percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation
Pubovaginal autologous fascial sling
explanation:
Refractory urgency incontinence is leakage associated with compelling urgency despite conservative and drug treatment. **Percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation** offers minimally invasive neuromodulation without reconstructing the outlet.

**A. Bladder neck suspension.** This improves mechanical support for stress leakage.
**B. Periurethral collagen.** Bulking improves urethral coaptation and targets stress incontinence.
**C. Tibial nerve stimulation.** Stimulation through a needle near the ankle modulates pathways involved in bladder storage.
**D. Fascial sling.** A sling supports the urethra against rises in abdominal pressure. Urgency is the problem described here.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 714.

q: A 67-year-old woman takes an aromatase inhibitor for breast cancer. Which effect described by Hazzard warrants fracture-risk assessment?
o: Decreased osteoporosis risk and decreased bone fracture risk
Increased osteoporosis risk and decreased bone fracture risk
Increased osteoporosis risk and increased bone fracture risk
Decreased osteoporosis risk and increased bone fracture risk
explanation:
Aromatase inhibitors reduce estrogen production in postmenopausal women. **Both osteoporosis and fragility fractures become more likely, so assess bone health and fracture risk.**

**A. Less osteoporosis and fewer fractures** — Estrogen depletion accelerates bone loss, so neither risk is expected to fall.
**B. More osteoporosis but fewer fractures** — The loss of bone strength increases susceptibility to a fracture after a low-energy fall.
**C. More osteoporosis and more fractures** — Assess baseline risks and bone density, encourage appropriate exercise, and consider bone-directed therapy when indicated.
**D. Less osteoporosis but more fractures** — The proposed reduction in osteoporosis reverses the skeletal effect of aromatase inhibition.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1390, Hormonal therapy.
ref: Hazzard Ch 88 — CANCER AND AGING: GENERAL PRINCIPLES

q: A 68-year-old man underwent kidney transplantation five years ago and takes tacrolimus, mycophenolate, and prednisone 5 mg daily. Three days ago, burning pain developed on the right chest, followed by vesicles in the T4–T6 dermatomes. Which mechanism most likely explains this presentation?
o: Primary infection with varicella-zoster virus following a new exposure.
Reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus with impaired cellular immunity.
Bacterial infection superimposed on a pre-existing inflammatory dermatitis.
Drug-induced photosensitivity producing an inflammatory eruption on exposed skin.
explanation:
Shingles typically presents with pain followed by grouped vesicles in a dermatomal distribution. In this immunosuppressed transplant recipient, **reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus as cellular immune control declines** fits the course.

**A. Primary varicella.** First infection typically causes a generalized chickenpox eruption rather than localized dermatomal pain and vesicles.
**B. Reactivation.** Cell-mediated immunity normally restrains latent VZV. Immunosuppression increases susceptibility to zoster.
**C. Bacterial superinfection.** It can complicate damaged skin but does not explain the characteristic initial pain and dermatomal vesicles.
**D. Photosensitivity.** A photosensitive eruption follows light exposure rather than a cluster of adjacent thoracic dermatomes.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1724–1725.
ref: Hazzard Ch 107 — OTHER VIRUSES: HUMAN IMMUNODEFICIENCY VIRUS INFECTION AND HERPES ZOSTER
chapterTitle: Other Viruses: Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection and Herpes Zoster

q: A 77-year-old woman with COPD and knee osteoarthritis has persistent knee pain despite acetaminophen. She has fallen twice this month and attributes this to knee pain. She takes tiotropium, albuterol, calcium, and vitamin D, has an MMSE score of 28/30, uses a walker, and has creatinine clearance of 38 mL/min. Which pharmacologic step follows Hazzard’s approach before oral NSAIDs or opioid escalation?
o: Apply topical diclofenac to the painful knee joints
Begin oral tramadol for the persistent knee pain
Begin oral celecoxib for the persistent knee pain
Begin oral hydrocodone with acetaminophen for knee pain
explanation:
Topical NSAIDs provide local pain relief for knee osteoarthritis with less systemic exposure than oral agents. **Try topical diclofenac on the painful knees** before escalating systemic treatment in a woman with falls and limited renal reserve.

**A. Topical diclofenac.** It targets the accessible joints while reducing exposure to systemic renal and sedative adverse effects.
**B. Oral tramadol.** Consider an opioid only in selected patients after other suitable options have failed.
**C. Oral celecoxib.** It still carries systemic renal and cardiovascular risks despite COX-2 selectivity.
**D. Hydrocodone with acetaminophen.** Sedation and falls are particular concerns, and total acetaminophen exposure also needs checking.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 787–788.

q: A 76-year-old woman has pruritus and vaginal discharge. Examination shows vulvar erythema and satellite lesions. Which microscopic finding and diagnosis match Hazzard's description?
o: Clue cells in vaginal fluid supporting candidiasis
Pseudohyphae in vaginal fluid supporting candidiasis
Pseudohyphae in vaginal fluid supporting bacterial vaginosis
Clue cells in vaginal fluid supporting estrogen-deficiency atrophy
explanation:
Itch, erythema and satellite lesions suggest vulvovaginal candidiasis. **Pseudohyphae on microscopy of vaginal fluid** support the diagnosis.

**A. Clue cells and candidiasis.** Clue cells are epithelial cells coated with bacteria and suggest bacterial vaginosis.
**B. Pseudohyphae and candidiasis.** The fungal structures fit both the examination and the suspected yeast infection.
**C. Pseudohyphae and bacterial vaginosis.** Bacterial vaginosis changes the vaginal bacterial flora. Pseudohyphae point toward yeast.
**D. Clue cells and estrogen deficiency.** Atrophy produces thin, pale mucosa. Clue cells indicate a bacterial-flora change.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 534.

q: An 86-year-old man with severe aortic stenosis, stage 3b CKD, and frailty (CFS 6) is offered TAVR. He uses a wheelchair, needs help with all IADLs, and receives continuous care from his wife. He wants comfort and to die at home when the time comes. His cardiologist emphasizes possible life prolongation; his wife is uncertain. What should the team do next?
o: Advance the TAVR plan based on stenosis severity before discussing his preferences
Arrange palliative care input to clarify goals before deciding about the procedure
Arrange direct hospice enrollment based on frailty before discussing procedural benefit
Attribute the comfort preference to depression and defer discussion for psychiatric review
explanation:
Deciding about TAVR requires weighing procedural benefit and burden against the patient's priorities. **Arrange goals-of-care discussion with palliative input before committing to the procedure**.

**A. Proceed on stenosis severity.** Severe stenosis does not determine whether treatment matches his goals.
**B. Clarify goals.** Ask how possible longer survival, function, comfort and time at home compare for him.
**C. Enroll in hospice on frailty alone.** Frailty informs prognosis but does not itself establish eligibility or preference.
**D. Assume depression.** A comfort preference can be valid and should be explored directly.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1052.
chapterTitle: Palliative Care and Special Management Issues
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · pp.1052, 1153

q: An 81-year-old man with carotid stenosis and significant heart disease is being assessed for intervention. Which consideration explains why transfemoral carotid stenting does not simply remove the procedural risks in this age group?
o: A higher perioperative stroke risk with endarterectomy than with transfemoral stenting
A lower perioperative stroke risk with transfemoral stenting among octogenarians
A higher perioperative stroke risk with transfemoral stenting among older patients
A lower perioperative myocardial infarction risk with endarterectomy than with stenting
explanation:
In older adults, a less invasive carotid procedure can exchange one hazard for another. **Transfemoral stenting carries greater perioperative stroke risk in older patients**, despite less procedural MI risk than open surgery.

**A. More stroke with endarterectomy.** The age-related stroke comparison usually favors endarterectomy over transfemoral stenting.
**B. Lower stenting stroke risk in octogenarians.** Older age strengthens the concern about stenting-associated stroke.
**C. Higher stenting stroke risk.** Weigh this against the individual's cardiac risk and anatomical suitability.
**D. Lower MI with endarterectomy.** Open surgery generally carries more perioperative MI risk than transfemoral stenting.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1214.

q: בתמונה 4 פצע לאחר שבועיים של טיפול מקומי להטריה אוטוליטית. לאור הממצא בשוליים, מהו הטיפול המומלץ כעת?
o: הטרייה כירורגית של הרקמה הלבנה ושימוש מקומי במשחה סטרואידלית
אפליקציה של METRONIDAZOLE מרוסק על השוליים וכיסוי בחבישה משנית
טיפול בהרטבות NaCl מספר פעמים ביום
שימוש בחבישה בעלת כושר ספיגה גדול
explanation:
Autolytic debridement retains moisture so the patient's enzymes can loosen devitalized tissue. A pale, softened rim around the wound indicates maceration when exudate sits against intact skin.

**Increase the dressing's absorptive capacity.** The goal is a moist wound bed with a protected margin, allowing excess fluid to move away from the surrounding skin.

**A. Excise the white rim and apply steroids.** The rim is consistent with macerated skin. Cutting it or applying a steroid does not correct the excess moisture.
**B. Crushed metronidazole on the edges.** Topical metronidazole is used for troublesome wound odor. Macerated margins call for moisture control.
**C. Repeated saline soaks.** More wetting leaves the surrounding skin exposed to fluid, even though saline can be appropriate for cleansing.
**D. More absorbent dressing.** Match absorption to drainage and reassess the edges. An alginate, hydrofiber or other suitable absorbent dressing can handle heavier output.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 693–694, Table 46-2.

q: מה נכון לגבי הטיפול ב- Hydralazine באי ספיקת לב?
o: מומלץ למטופלים שלא יכולים לסבול טיפול בחסמי ACE
מעלה תמותה
ניתן פעם ביום
קיימת קונטראינדיקציה לשילוב עם ניטרטים
explanation:
Hydralazine dilates resistance vessels, while a nitrate reduces venous return. **Hydralazine plus isosorbide dinitrate is an alternative for selected HFrEF patients unable to tolerate renin–angiotensin system therapy**.

**A. ACE inhibitor intolerance** The evidence concerns the combination. Consider why the ACE inhibitor cannot be used and whether an ARB or ARNI is suitable before choosing this alternative.
**B. Increases mortality** In A-HeFT the combined regimen improved survival in the population studied.
**C. Once-daily dosing** The heart-failure regimen uses multiple daily doses, which can affect adherence.
**D. Contraindicated with nitrates** A nitrate is the intended partner. Assess hypotension, headache and tolerability.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1181–1182. AHA/ACC/HFSA HF guideline (2022), §7.3.5.

q: בן 68 עם מחלת פרקינסון, שאובחנה לפני 6 שנים, מתמודד עם קושי הולך וגובר בזיכרון, קשב וקבלת החלטות. התסמינים המוטוריים של החולה יציבים, אך הירידה הקוגניטיבית הפכה בולטת יותר במהלך 6 החודשים האחרונים, מלווה בירידה בקשב, הפרעת שינה וליקוי ויזו-מרחבי. איזו מהאפשרויות הבאות היא אופציה טיפולית של קו ראשון לטיפול בתסמינים של המטופל?
o: Levodopa
Cholinesterase Inhibitors
Dopamine Agonists
Antipsychotics
explanation:
Dementia beginning years after established Parkinson disease fits Parkinson disease dementia. **A cholinesterase inhibitor**, particularly rivastigmine, is an option for cognitive symptoms.

**A. Levodopa.** It treats motor symptoms and is not first-line treatment for cognitive decline.
**B. Cholinesterase inhibitors.** Increasing central cholinergic transmission may modestly improve cognition or function.
**C. Dopamine agonists.** These target motor symptoms and may worsen hallucinations or confusion.
**D. Antipsychotics.** These are not cognitive enhancers and can worsen parkinsonism or cause other serious harms.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 870, 939, 947–948, 984.
chapterTitle: Cognitive Changes in Normal and Pathologic Aging
referenceNote: Printed IMA citation retained; checked explanation source: Hazzard 8e · p. 947.

q: An older adult with symptomatic knee osteoarthritis asks how conservative treatment and joint replacement fit together. Which account follows Hazzard?
o: Medication modifies disease progression, while nonpharmacologic treatment is directed toward relief of symptoms.
Joint replacement precedes conservative treatment, which is introduced afterward for persistent symptomatic disease.
Conservative therapies target symptoms, with joint replacement considered when these treatments have failed.
Disease-modifying medication is the next treatment step when conservative symptom management has failed.
explanation:
Osteoarthritis treatment aims to reduce pain and preserve function. **Use nonpharmacologic and pharmacologic conservative treatment first, then consider joint replacement for persistent disabling symptoms**.

**A. Medicine modifies progression.** Routine OA medicines chiefly improve symptoms and do not reliably reverse structural progression.
**B. Replace the joint first.** Surgery is generally considered after appropriate conservative care fails and symptoms justify its risks.
**C. Conservative care then possible replacement.** Combine exercise and other physical measures with appropriate analgesia and reassess function.
**D. Escalate to a disease-modifying OA drug.** There is no established disease-modifying drug analogous to those used for inflammatory arthritis.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 779.

q: In managing myxedema coma, what is the critical sequencing error to avoid regarding hydrocortisone and thyroid hormone?
o: Initiating hydrocortisone to cover potentially impaired adrenal reserve
Giving thyroid hormone without hydrocortisone when adrenal reserve is impaired
Obtaining serum for cortisol measurement before starting hydrocortisone
Stopping hydrocortisone after the cortisol level is found adequate
explanation:
Profound hypothyroidism can coexist with impaired adrenal reserve. **Avoid giving thyroid hormone without hydrocortisone when that reserve may be inadequate.**

**A. Start hydrocortisone** Empirical IV cover protects against adrenal crisis while the cortisol result is pending.
**B. Give thyroid hormone alone** Thyroid replacement can precipitate adrenal crisis if cortisol availability is inadequate.
**C. Obtain pretreatment cortisol** A blood sample before hydrocortisone allows subsequent interpretation and should be taken promptly.
**D. Stop cover after an adequate cortisol result** Once cortisol is adequate, continuing empirical hydrocortisone is unnecessary.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1553, Myxedema coma treatment.

בן 82 מגיע למיון בעקבות בלבול חריף ועצירות. בבדיקות מעבדה:

באק"ג: סינוס 76 פעימות בדקה, QT מקוצר.
מה הטיפול הראשוני המומלץ?
o: דיאליזה
טיפול ב -FUROSEMIDE

keySource: IMA 2025-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q106
explanation:
Hypercalcemia can cause polyuria and volume depletion, which further reduces renal calcium clearance. **Begin IV isotonic saline**, with careful reassessment of cardiac and renal tolerance.

**A. Dialysis.** Dialysis is reserved for selected severe or refractory cases or when fluids cannot be given safely.
**B. Furosemide first.** A loop diuretic before rehydration can worsen depletion. It may be needed for volume overload after fluids.
**C. Intravenous 0.9% saline.** Restoring intravascular volume improves filtration and urinary calcium clearance.
**D. Zoledronic acid first.** An antiresorptive can follow or accompany hydration when indicated, but its onset is delayed and it does not correct volume depletion.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 364–365.

q: מה השילוב הנכון בין סוג הזיהום העורי לבין חיידק הגורם לו בשכיחות גבוהה?
o: Folliculitis נגרם על ידי Staph aureus
Necrotizing fasciitis נגרם על ידי Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Hand-foot-and-mouth disease נגרם על ידי Parapoxvirus
Erysipelas נגרם על ידי Mycobacterium marinum
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 134 – Infections of the Skin, Muscles, and Soft Tissues
keySource: IMA 2022-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q119
explanation:
Folliculitis is infection or inflammation centered on a hair follicle. **Staphylococcus aureus is a frequent bacterial cause** of ordinary folliculitis.

**A. Folliculitis and S. aureus.** Tender follicle-centered pustules fit staphylococcal disease. Hot-tub exposure suggests a different bacterial cause.
**B. Necrotizing fasciitis and Pseudomonas.** The usual associations include group A streptococci or mixed aerobic–anaerobic organisms.
**C. Hand-foot-and-mouth disease and parapoxvirus.** Coxsackie and other enteroviruses cause hand-foot-and-mouth disease. Parapoxviruses cause distinct lesions such as orf.
**D. Erysipelas and M. marinum.** Erysipelas is usually streptococcal. M. marinum more often causes nodular cutaneous disease after aquatic exposure.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 1049–1051.

q: מה המהימנות של בדיקת מיפוי ריאות לאבחנת תסחיף ריאתי חד?
o: תשובת מיפוי תקינה שוללת תסחיף ב-90% מהמקרים
בתשובת מיפוי של סבירות גבוהה, הסיכון לתסחיף הוא מעל 90%
לרוב ניתן לקבל תשובה ברורה מתוצאות המיפוי
ברוב הנבדקים עם תסחיף תהיה סבירות גבוהה במיפוי
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 290 – Deep-Venous Thrombosis and Pulmonary Thromboembolism
keySource: IMA 2022-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q139
explanation:
Ventilation–perfusion imaging changes PE probability in light of clinical pretest probability. **A high-probability scan with high clinical probability gives a likelihood above 90%**. The scan label alone does not carry a fixed positive predictive value in every population.

**A. Normal excludes only 90%.** A normal perfusion scan has stronger exclusionary value and essentially rules out acute PE in the usual diagnostic setting.
**B. High-probability scan.** With concordant high clinical probability, the reported likelihood was about 96%. Discordance requires further assessment.
**C. Most scans definitive.** Conventional planar V/Q imaging frequently yields an intermediate or nondiagnostic result.
**D. Most PE cases have a high-probability scan.** High positive predictive value is distinct from sensitivity. Many confirmed emboli lack a high-probability pattern.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1519. Lavorini et al., Multidisciplinary Respiratory Medicine 2013, article 75.
Key note: The accepted option gives a likelihood above 90% for a high-probability scan alone. The 96% figure in Hazzard requires concordant high clinical probability.
